correctness.rationale: The 64 published line equations permit an exact determinant test for all 2016 pairs. The package additionally certifies an exact squarefree degree-five annihilating polynomial and five trace moments, which uniquely determine the eigenvalue multiplicities because the adjacency matrix is symmetric. Shifting by -2 is correct for the line-intersection matrix on a smooth quartic K3 surface.

value.rationale: The Schur quartic is the extremal smooth complex quartic for line count. Exact spectrum, inertia and transversal-profile data are natural structural invariants that refine the well-known rank and regularity facts and can support future symmetry, lattice and incidence analyses.
residual_risks: A specialized graph database or unindexed computational note could contain the same exact spectrum without terminology exposed by the searches.

final_claim: The intersection graph of the 64 lines on the Segre–Schur quartic is connected, 18-regular and diameter two with adjacency spectrum 18^1, 2^44, (-4)^8, (-6)^9, (-10)^2; its adjacent and skew pairs have the stated complete common-neighbor frequency profile, and the shifted line-intersection matrix therefore has rank 20 and inertia (1,19,44).
limitations: A fixed-configuration exact theorem; no classification of spectra for other quartic surfaces is claimed.
The common-neighbor counts are not claimed to coincide with automorphism-orbit classes.
